text: A newborn calf can be held by one person, but a 6-month-old calf needs two people. For adults: tying with a rope to a tree is traditional but unsafe and impractical for anything beyond a single quick injection; firmly holding the head by the nose can restrict movement but only works on quiet, not-too-large animals; various rudimentary restraint setups are also used. The best and safest option is building a crush — a modest investment that can be shared between several farmers, and one that makes farmers and veterinarians much more willing to handle cattle for routine care. To lay an adult animal down safely and with minimal stress, a rope of about 10 meters is needed.
